intro: A probability estimate should distinguish its center from its uncertainty. Beta conjugacy updates both using observed successes and failures.
task: Return posterior Beta parameters, posterior mean, and posterior variance after binary observations.
requirements: alpha and beta are scalars in [1e-8,1e6]. successes and failures are integers in [0,1000000].
Set a=alpha+successes and b=beta+failures. Return {"alpha": a, "beta": b, "mean": a/(a+b), "variance": a*b/((a+b)**2*(a+b+1))}.
Return posterior uncertainty about the unknown success probability, not the Bernoulli variance of the next binary observation. Zero observations retain the prior.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Uniform prior and one success
examples.output:
{
  "alpha": 2,
  "beta": 1,
  "mean": 0.66666667,
  "variance": 0.05555556
}
(Arrays shown as lists; numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places.)

examples.name: No observations
examples.output:
{
  "alpha": 1,
  "beta": 1,
  "mean": 0.5,
  "variance": 0.08333333
}
(Arrays shown as lists; numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places.)

examples.name: Balanced evidence
examples.output:
{
  "alpha": 5,
  "beta": 5,
  "mean": 0.5,
  "variance": 0.02272727
}
(Arrays shown as lists; numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places.)

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Treat success and failure counts as additions to different concentration parameters.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Compute the posterior parameter variance separately from the variance of a single future binary draw.

explanation: Successes add to alpha and failures add to beta. The posterior mean moves toward the observed success fraction, while the total concentration records how much evidence supports that center.
Two Beta distributions can share the same mean and have different variances. The posterior variance describes uncertainty about a probability parameter, not variability of a single future outcome.
